name: Launch Handler
plain: Controls how an installed app reopens when a link is clicked.
meaning: Picks reuse of the existing window or a new one.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Controls how an installed app reopens when a link is clicked.

limits.headline: Can choose whether links reopen your installed app in its existing window or a new one
limits.user_action: You click a link that opens in your installed web app
can: Reuse the app's open window when you click a link
Pass the link to the app that is already running
cannot: Work for a site that is not installed
Open links outside the app on its own
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet only. Firefox, Safari and iPhone do not support it.

story.what_it_is: An installed web app picks whether a clicked link reuses its open window or opens a new one.

marketing.name: launch_handler
marketing.pitch: A setting that tells an installed web app how to open when launched, such as reusing an existing window.

story.for_you: You click a link to your app, and it opens in the window you already have, instead of a pile of new windows. It feels tidy and like a normal desktop app.
story.for_makers: Makers choose between single window and many windows for a better flow. A chat app can jump to the right thread in the open window. It is a polish feature for installed web apps.

use_cases.example: A chat app takes you to the right conversation in the window you already have open.
A web music player plays the clicked track in the existing player, not a second one.
A web mail app opens a new message in the main window when you click a mail link.
A web game launcher reuses its window when you click a game invite link.
A web video call app takes your meeting link to the call window you already have.
A web design app opens a shared file link in its existing window as a new tab.
A company portal opens a link to a ticket in the same app window to keep staff focused.
